problem: Determine the largest union of intervals on which the function $f(x)=-\frac{2{x}^{3}}{2x+16}$ is continuous.
worked_solution:
This is a rational function, so it is continuous at all points in its domain. To find its domain, we start by factoring the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =-\frac{2{x}^{3}}{2x+16} \\  & =-\frac{2{x}^{3}}{2(x+8)} \\  & =-\frac{{x}^{3}}{x+8}\end{aligned}
$$

 

This function is continuous everywhere except at the excluded point $x=-8.$

Therefore, the domain consists of the union of the intervals $(-\infty ,-8)$ and $(-8,\infty ),$ namely

$$
(-\infty ,-8)\cup (-8,\infty )
$$

and the function is also continuous on these intervals.
